description.narrative:
PUI is a multi-sectoral humanitarian organization that works in hard-to-reach areas in humanitarian crises, often on the frontline and builds its work on health and nutrition interventions. PUI is active in about 20 countries, the majority of which are listed in the ACAPS Humanitarian Access Overview as contexts with high, very high or extreme restrictions on humanitarian access. About 40% of PUI's activities are focused on health. PUI also works in the areas of nutrition, food security and livelihoods, water, sanitation and hygiene, protection and mental health and psychosocial support. The organization reaches about six million people per year.
Sida entered into an agreement with PUI for the first time in 2023-2025 and now for the second time in 2026-2029. PUI is considered to provide added value to Sida's humanitarian portfolio as an agile and responsive humanitarian actor with access to areas and groups with the most severe humanitarian needs that other humanitarian actors do not reach.

PUI är en multi-sektoriell humanitär organisation som arbetar i svårtillgängliga områden i humanitära kriser, ofta i frontlinjen och utgår ifrån hälsa och nutritions interventioner. PUI är verksamma i ca 20 länder varav majoriteten är listade i ACAPS Humanitarian Access Overview som kontexter med höga, mycket höga eller extrema begränsningar i humanitärt tillträde. Omkring ca 40% av PUI:s verksamhet är inriktad på hälsa. PUI arbetar också inom områdena nutrition, tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning och uppehälle, vatten, sanitet och hygien, skydd samt psykisk hälsa och psykosocialt stöd. Organisationen når cirka sex miljoner människor per år.
Sida ingick avtal med PUI första gången 2023-2025 och nu för andra gången 2026-2029. PUI anses ge ett mervärde till Sidas humanitära portfölj som en agil och responsiv humanitär aktör med tillträde till områden och grupper med de mest allvarliga humanitära behoven som andra humanitära aktörer inte når.

Première Urgence Internationale's (PUI) main commitment, as per their charter, is to provide assistance, to relieve and preserve lives by carrying out humanitarian and development actions throughout the world, without any discrimination, in favour of civilian victims, endangered, marginalized or excluded by the effects of armed conflicts, natural disasters or economic collapse following political upheaval or the consequences of environmental and climatic degradation. PUI is a principled humanitarian organisation with the aim of doing so through a multi-sectoral response focusing of the sectors of Health, Nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), Protection and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS).
Health remains PUI's main sector of intervention through which other sectors are built in, as part of the integrated approach which is a strength given health is often perceived as neutral. The objectives for each sectoral intervention is outlined in the interventions frameworks for each sector with a theory of change for each sector. Below is a summary of the overall objective or objectives of each sector. As these are the overall frameworks for PUI's management, it gives a view of what PUI strives towards in interventions including these sector interventions. In order to understand the design of PUI's projects and assess PUI's context specific objectives the theory for each project intervention can be found in the Full Project Proposals, that are shared and approved by Sida annually.
The overall objective of PUI's public health intervention framework is to support communities and health systems in responding to priority public health problems, thereby helping to reduce mortality and morbidity.
In regards to WASH PUI's three objectives are; - to ensure survival in vulnerable populations by quickly improving their conditions for life, establishing their access to water and essential environmental and sanitary conditions; - to assist in reducing rates of morbidity and mortality through providing adequate access to facilities intended for the provision of water and sanitation. This is to be achieved through engaging with and mobilising the local community; - to support the health and well-being of populations by improving management of services for drinking water, basic sanitation and environmental protection and through WASH interventions, assist in improving the capacity of the local population to prevent emergency situations arising and their capacity to be resilient after a shock/crisis does occur.
In regards to food and nutrition security and livelihoods PUI's four objectives are; - to ensure survival by immediately improving living conditions for the most vulnerable by giving them access to food and supplying basic goods and social services. - to ensure the protection and the restoration of vulnerable peoples livelihoods by empowering them to access basic social services and goods and by promoting economic opportunities. - to prevent the degradation of peoples livelihoods and strengthening them in a sustainable way through better resource management, further integration into market systems and social cohesion. - to produce and improve access to high-quality information at local and national level for a better coordination and humanitarian response.
PUI's work with protection builds on the three objectives; - to contribute to the collective humanitarian protection responsibility and outcomes by systematically incorporating protection principles within all PUIs interventions, regardless of the context or sector of intervention. - to contribute to the promotion and protection of the rights of crisis-affected populations through integrated protection responses. - to contribute to the prevention, reduction, and response to violence, coercion, deliberate deprivation and abuse for persons, groups, and communities affected by humanitarian crises.
In relation to MHPSS, PUI's overall objective is to contribute to the collective humanitarian protection responsibility and outcomes by incorporating MHPSS transversal approach to protection principles within all relevant PUIs interventions.
